title: Pharmaceutical water technical notes | Aquemi
meta: Answer-first notes on USP <645>, <1231>, Ph. Eur. 12.3, EU GMP Annex 1, ASME BPE and CSA B51 for PW, WFI and pure steam. Get each one by email.
eyebrow: TECHNICAL NOTES · PW · WFI · PURE STEAM
headline: Water system questions, answered in the first three sentences
lead: Notes for engineering, validation and quality teams running Purified Water (PW), Water for Injection (WFI) and pure steam systems. Each answers one question first and names its clause. None is published yet.

blocks.intro: What a clause asks, and what a new edition changes. Each row links to the page where we apply the answer.

items.q: How is each note written and reviewed?
items.a: A named Aquemi engineer writes it from a question we are asked on projects, and a second engineer checks it before publication. Each claim names the standard, clause and edition; numbers carry their units. The note shows its publication date and date of last review. [Named author for each topic group]

items.q: Can we cite a note in our validation documents?
items.a: Cite the standard, not the note. A note is our reading of the clause, with the clause number so you can check it. Your quality unit decides how the standard applies to your site.

items.q: What happens when a standard changes after a note is published?
items.a: We review the note against the new text, update it and change its date of last review. If the answer changes, the note says what changed and when, and subscribers to that topic get the update. Errors are fixed in place with a dated correction line, never silently.

Not yet. We will post FAT and handover milestones only with the client's written permission, and changes to our facilities, people and certifications that affect your projects. Each item carries its date; project news links to its case study.

items.q: Our question is about our own system, not a general one.
items.a: Send it through the proposal or service request form, so an engineer can answer it against your documents. We only turn questions into notes when the answer holds for most systems.
